lines: Implemented and critically audited against uml.tool_jobs.python and uml.tool_jobs.contract. Python now uses the existing Chat-owned process registry: python_start returns immediately with optional stdin; ordinary python uses a soft initial wait capped at ten seconds when output/input/stop/list are frozen. Both retain frozen interpreter and approval authority; managed Python adds -u alongside -I for live output. Shared controls, owner isolation, final-answer gate, stop, output cursors, restart/no-replay and hidden Windows console behavior apply without a separate Python lifecycle. Legacy Python without controls retains its original argv and hard timeout; python_start without controls fails before launch. Shared job labels and documentation cover both languages.

Verification: desktop Rust library 347 passed; host milestone_05 14, process_sessions 3, python_adapter 2 passed (one process fixture intentionally ignored). TypeScript check, Vite build, native desktop build and git diff --check passed. Actual isolated projectless Windows WebView test with C:\Python313\python.exe passed 18 provider requests: approval resume, premature-final reminder, unbuffered print and stdin, sys.flags.isolated=1, GetConsoleWindow=0, retained job across inputs, ordinary soft yield, complete tree stop, root exit with live descendant followed by verified treeEmpty, missing-controls rejection, legacy hard timeout. Evidence: desktop/src-tauri/target/native-python-jobs-1789665154584/requests.json and verified.png. Existing shell native regression passed 11 requests: desktop/src-tauri/target/native-shell-jobs-1789665193780. Test apps clean their own process trees. No Adashi QA changes. Windows verified; no new native Linux/macOS execution claim. Generated architecture projections and .adashi state updated by Adashi. No outstanding implementation blocker; task finished for review.

data.description: Implement python_start and normal Python soft waits through the existing Chat-owned job registry. Preserve frozen interpreter, approvals, legacy Chats without job controls, isolation validation and cancellation. Support incremental unbuffered output, stdin, tree stop, final-response nudge, restart semantics, and no console window. Verify Rust contracts and real native projectless Chat lifecycle; no Adashi QA changes.
data.title: Extend managed process jobs to the Python tool
